messages.author: 248af1cd72d9f2d5
messages.subject: Object symmetry
parts:
Hi everyone,

I want to perform object symmetry on my data (with semi landmarks) so used gpagen before using bilat.symmetry to specify that I would like object symmetry. All this works fine but I am unable to access my csize on the outputted symmetric data, which I would like to use for the rest of my analysis. 

Is there a way to access centroid size from the symmetric component of my data? I noticed in a previous discussion (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/geomorph-r-package/centroid$20size$20symmetry%7Csort:date/geomorph-r-package/lAvr9F_LQB8/kAn61_yfBQAJ) that the function does not yet output the size components. If this is still the case, am I right in thinking that I can manually extract csize after using bilateral.symmetry?

I also had 4 replicates per individual and I noticed that bilat.symmetry may actually group these replicates automatically, is this the case? If not then would you recommend taking the mean of these groups before or after superimposition? 

Sorry for the basic questions...I have read around and can't seem to find any answers so have turned to this forum, at risk of asking what may potentially be considered obvious!

Thanks,
Sam

messages.author: f16866fc42d43e64
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Object symmetry
parts:
Hi Sam,

 

Bilat.symmetry does not output sizes, but you already have them as output from gpagen. For matching symmetry evaluating symmetric and asymmetric shape (and size) makes sense as there are two objects being compared. However, for object symmetry there is a single size per individual, so it is unclear what the symmetric and asymmetric size components would represent in this case. This is why the size anova is not computed in bilat.symmetry for object symmetry.

 

As for replicates, using 4 per individual is fine; a vector specifying them is provided in the replicate = argument of the function. If you then want to calculate a mean for each individual for other shape analyses, you need to do so on superimposed coordinates.

 

Hope this helps.

Hey Antigoni,

Thanks for your answers :-) and yes they definitely do help!

I ended up getting different lengths due to replicates being in gpagen$Csize but not symm.shape (due to inclusion of reps in Csize). So I took the mean of both gpagen$coords and gpagen$Csize (after superimposition) and made a new gdf. However, after I conducted bilat.symmetry the image was reflected completely (ie. left to right) instead of just being reflected across the specified co-ordinate axis.

Any ideas as to why this could happen? Everything was working fine before I averaged by group, but just in case I have included parts of my code below.

Thanks again,
Sam




ind.shape <- coords.subset(gdf$shape, gdf$ind)
means <- lapply(ind.shape, mshape) 
shape.means <- simplify2array(means)

apdlm.csize <- advanced.procD.lm(Csize ~ ind, ~1, groups = ~ind, iter=1, data = gdf)
Csize.means <- apdlm.csize$LS.means

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape = shape.means, ind = ind)

# bilateral.symmetry
lands.objSym <- bilat.symmetry(A = shape, ind = ind, 
                               object.sym = TRUE, land.pairs = land.pairs,
                               RRPP = TRUE, iter = 500, data = gdf)

messages.author: f16866fc42d43e64
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Object symmetry
parts:
Sam, 

I am not sure that fully averaging your shape data before testing for asymmetry is useful, as in that case you are not taking measurement error into account (please consult general bibliography on the study of FA, and the references cited in the function´s help file as to why one generally wants to take ME into account when testing for asymmetry).

As for the reflection of data you mentioned, it is not clear to me what image you are referring to or what you are thinking about when talking about a "specified co-ordinate axis". During object asymmetry tests, the studied structure is reflected as a means of estimating the side effect, but that is not something you actually "see" in the result of the function.

Cheers,
Antigoni

Bilat.symmetry does not output sizes, but you already have them as output from gpagen. For matching symmetry evaluating symmetric and asymmetric shape (and size) makes sense as there are two objects being compared. However, for object symmetry there is a single size per individual, so it is unclear what the symmetric and asymmetric size components would represent in this case. This is why the size anova is not computed in bilat.symmetry for object symmetry.

 

As for replicates, using 4 per individual is fine; a vector specifying them is provided in the replicate = argument of the function. If you then want to calculate a mean for each individual for other shape analyses, you need to do so on superimposed coordinates.

 

Hope this helps.



On Wed, Feb 21, 2018 at 9:28 AM, svb <be...@mail.holar.is> wrote:
Hi everyone,

I want to perform object symmetry on my data (with semi landmarks) so used gpagen before using bilat.symmetry to specify that I would like object symmetry. All this works fine but I am unable to access my csize on the outputted symmetric data, which I would like to use for the rest of my analysis. 

Is there a way to access centroid size from the symmetric component of my data? I noticed in a previous discussion (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/geomorph-r-package/centroid$20size$20symmetry%7Csort:date/geomorph-r-package/lAvr9F_LQB8/kAn61_yfBQAJ) that the function does not yet output the size components. If this is still the case, am I right in thinking that I can manually extract csize after using bilateral.symmetry?

I also had 4 replicates per individual and I noticed that bilat.symmetry may actually group these replicates automatically, is this the case? If not then would you recommend taking the mean of these groups before or after superimposition? 

Sorry for the basic questions...I have read around and can't seem to find any answers so have turned to this forum, at risk of asking what may potentially be considered obvious!

Thanks,
Sam

parts:
Hi Antigoni,

I went back to this thread as (some of) my plots from bilat.symmetry are being reflected (i.e. pointing specimens pointing to the right and not to the left as it should be) when I have specified 'object.sym = TRUE', as well as giving 'land.pairs'. However, in other populations, plotting bilat.symmetry works with no problem (i.e. all specimens remain pointing to the left), and I use exactly the same code. I also find no real differences between my TPS files and classifier files between populations. Do you know what else might be causing this?

Thanks,
Sam


gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape = gpa.res.before$coords,
                           ind = as.factor(classifierBefore$ID),
                           size = as.numeric(as.character(classifierBefore$size)),
                           female = as.factor(classifierBefore$female))

# object symmetry using the shape output performed from gpagen (as this includes semilandmarks)
lands.objSym <- bilat.symmetry(A = shape, ind = ind, replicate = rep,

object.sym = TRUE, land.pairs = land.pairs,
                               RRPP = TRUE, iter = 500, data = gdf)
On Friday, 23 February 2018 07:42:54 UTC, Antigoni Kaliontzopoulou wrote:
Yes, that is correct.
On Fri, Feb 23, 2018 at 6:58 AM, Samantha Victoria Beck <be...@mail.holar.is> wrote:

Hi Antigoni,

Thanks for this. So taking the average of centroid size from gpagen and using it within procD.lm with shape coords outputted from bilat.symmetry is correct to do?

Cheers,
Sam
On 21 February 2018 at 15:42, Antigoni Kaliontzopoulou <ant...@gmail.com> wrote:

Sam, 

I am not sure that fully averaging your shape data before testing for asymmetry is useful, as in that case you are not taking measurement error into account (please consult general bibliography on the study of FA, and the references cited in the function´s help file as to why one generally wants to take ME into account when testing for asymmetry).

As for the reflection of data you mentioned, it is not clear to me what image you are referring to or what you are thinking about when talking about a "specified co-ordinate axis". During object asymmetry tests, the studied structure is reflected as a means of estimating the side effect, but that is not something you actually "see" in the result of the function.

Cheers,
Antigoni
On Wed, Feb 21, 2018 at 2:11 PM, Samantha Victoria Beck <be...@mail.holar.is> wrote:

Hey Antigoni,

Thanks for your answers :-) and yes they definitely do help!

I ended up getting different lengths due to replicates being in gpagen$Csize but not symm.shape (due to inclusion of reps in Csize). So I took the mean of both gpagen$coords and gpagen$Csize (after superimposition) and made a new gdf. However, after I conducted bilat.symmetry the image was reflected completely (ie. left to right) instead of just being reflected across the specified co-ordinate axis.

Any ideas as to why this could happen? Everything was working fine before I averaged by group, but just in case I have included parts of my code below.

Thanks again,
Sam




ind.shape <- coords.subset(gdf$shape, gdf$ind)
means <- lapply(ind.shape, mshape) 
shape.means <- simplify2array(means)

apdlm.csize <- advanced.procD.lm(Csize ~ ind, ~1, groups = ~ind, iter=1, data = gdf)
Csize.means <- apdlm.csize$LS.means

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape = shape.means, ind = ind)

# bilateral.symmetry
lands.objSym <- bilat.symmetry(A = shape, ind = ind, 
                               object.sym = TRUE, land.pairs = land.pairs,
                               RRPP = TRUE, iter = 500, data = gdf)
